text: Most agent demos show the happy path — user asks, agent succeeds. That's table stakes. What makes this capstone worth presenting is everything on top of it: the rejection path, a stopping condition actually firing, a real audit log entry.

One sentence ties it together: a tool-using agent with a human-approval checkpoint on its one consequential action, backed by append-only logging, iteration and cost limits, and least-privilege credentials — verified working, not just demoed. Every clause in that sentence is a lesson you can speak to.

When you present it, don't just show success. Show a human declining the refund and the agent handling it gracefully. Show a stopping condition firing. Show the audit log from a real run. That's what a working interviewer who builds agents has rarely seen a candidate actually demonstrate.

This is the eighth of twelve courses in the AI Engineer path's Job-Ready stage. Next up, Azure AI and Cloud for AI Engineers, picks up exactly where deployment left off — running agents like this one in a real cloud environment, including Azure AI Foundry, Azure OpenAI, and Azure AI Search.
Six chapters, one small agent, every control real. That's AI Agents, done. See you in Azure AI and Cloud for AI Engineers.
